title: Rabbi Akiva's Water in Prison
summary: The three doors of Gehinnom, in the desert, in the sea and in Yerushalayim, and the three ways a person ends up there; the smoke between two palm trees in Gei Ben Hinnom; and Gehinnom's seven names. Then where the door to Gan Eden is, the Torah that is "longer than the earth," the two baskets of figs, "new and old I have stored for you," and why the words of the Sofrim must be guarded even more than the Torah's. It ends with Rabbi Akiva in prison, who used his last water to wash his hands.
key_ideas: The doors to Gehinnom are the ways a person gets there: through speech, through what he does, and through a lack of fear of Heaven.
No place or time is an excuse; a person can sin even in Yerushalayim, and do good even in hard times.
Be careful with the mitzvos of the Rabbanan even more than with those of the Torah.
Rabbi Akiva gave his last water to wash his hands rather than drink.
